title: Introduce cross-horizon fingerprint controller and traffic-aware rollback gate
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Several recent canary regressions were short-lived and localized to traffic subcohorts or phase shifts; existing detectors either reacted too slowly or overreacted to noisy microbursts. This PR implements a cross-horizon fingerprint controller (CHFC) that fuses multiscale latency/throughput fingerprints across temporal horizons and traffic partitions to produce a stable drift signal and a traffic-aware rollback gate. Key behaviours: 1) Multiscale fusion: CHFC computes short/medium/long horizon fingerprints per traffic cohort and uses a weighted Bayesian fusion to estimate persistent regressions versus transient noise. 2) Traffic-aware weighting: fusion weights adapt to cohort size, traffic modality (sampling-heavy vs. bursty), and concurrency slice so small cohorts do not dominate global decisions. 3) Reservoir with staleness decay: we introduce an epochal reservoir sampler per cohort with exponential staleness decay so older probes have less influence but are retained for trend continuity. 4) Safe rollback gate: the controller outputs a conservative rollback score and a confidence band; the rollout guard uses both the score and traffic-aware confidence to decide soft-fallback, staged pause, or immediate rollback. 5) Backpressure integration: when the controller detects correlated throughput degradation, it signals the throttler to temporarily reduce canary traffic and re-probe. Design notes and tradeoffs are described inline; the fusion algorithm favors false negatives slightly to avoid churn in high-frequency canaries. Implementation summary: - core controller in perf/canary/controller.go: 720 LOC; includes fusion engine, reservoir, and gating logic - metric adapter perf/adapter/horizon_adapter.go: converts aggregated telemetry into horizon fingerprints - config schema changes perf/config/cross_horizon.yaml: new tunables (horizon windows, decay tau, cohort weight priors, rollback thresholds) - CLI and console: perf-cli add chfc status/check commands; console dashboard cards for cross-horizon signal and cohort-level confidence - tests: unit tests for fusion math (perf/canary/controller_test.go), synthetic e2e replay harness (perf/canary/replay_e2e_test.py) validating graceful fallback under synthetic bursts Rollout plan: roll out as opt-in default for canary pipeline 2.0 with a four-step staged rollout: (1) opt-in on internal canaries, (2) enable for non-critical production canaries with monitoring-only mode, (3) enable active gating with conservative thresholds, (4) scale thresholds per team after 2 weeks of telemetry. Safety and observability: added tracing spans for controller decision path; exposed per-cohort confidence and reservoir health metrics (chfc.confidence, chfc.reservoir_size, chfc.staleness_penalty). Migration: existing canary pipelines will ignore CHFC unless enabled in canary spec. The config provides safe defaults that mirror current behaviour until teams reduce thresholds. Testing and validation: local unit coverage 92%; replay tests show 85-92% reduction in noisy rollbacks on historical datasets with negligible false negative increase. Benchmarks: controller adds ~3-6% CPU on canary evaluator nodes at 1000 rps; memory overhead per cohort ~12KB. Related work: builds on ENG-8219 (temporal-cohort fusion prototype) and leverages traffic shaping hooks from ENG-8033. References to internal runbooks: Linear ENG-8421 contains follow-up tuning tasks and post-deploy checks. Notes: tuned default priors to favor stability for small cohorts and provide a short-circuit in case of clear degradations. See release_notes for recommended threshold tweaks.

release_notes: Add cross-horizon fingerprint controller (CHFC) to canary pipelines. CHFC fuses multiscale latency/throughput fingerprints per traffic cohort to reduce noisy rollbacks and provide traffic-aware rollback gating. Opt-in via canary config 'chfc.enabled: true'. Defaults are conservative; teams should observe chfc.confidence and adjust 'rollback_threshold' as needed.
